Incident Bot: [ALERT] 03/14/2026 09:01:08 UTC — high KV cache memory growth and continuous-batching latency spikes detected in runtime-cluster-eu-west-1. Affected models: mistral-2.2-mqa, qwen-1.3-gqa. Error rate elevated. Paging SRE team. Pager: @emily_oncall :rotating_light:
Emily (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing sustained mem growth on nodes serving mistral-2.2-mqa, top of stack shows kv-cache size increasing ~15GB in 10m. Suspect prefix churn + continuous batching. Any recent releases?
Javier (ML Infra): Hi — there was a small batching heuristic tweak in yesterday's runtime release (rev 2026.03.14-b2) that changed continuous batching thresholds for MQA models to be more aggressive. Reverting might help.
Ingrid (Platform Eng): Logs show a flurry of unique prefix keys from a handful of clients -> KV key cardinality spike. Example trace:```
[2026-03-14T09:00:52Z] model=mistral-2.2-mqa req_id=abc123 prefix_hash=0x7f4a... kv_cache_len=124567
[2026-03-14T09:01:01Z] model=qwen-1.3-gqa req_id=def456 prefix_hash=0x9b2c... kv_cache_len=130214
OOM warning: process killed due to RSS>90%
```
Emily (oncall): Customer impact? Ben? Customer Ops?
Ben (Support): Seeing multiple support tickets starting 08:58 UTC for timeouts / partial responses from customers using MQA/GQA endpoints. Two customers on Dedicated reported high error rate for streaming responses. No PII exposed.
Customer Ops: Quick summary for execs: ~7% of hosted traffic to those models is affected in EU region, errors primarily timeout/partial streams, start time ~08:58 UTC. Potentially wider if not mitigated.
Javier (ML Infra): Proposed mitigation steps:
1) Disable continuous batching for suspected model variants (mistral-2.2-mqa, qwen-1.3-gqa)
2) Reduce max_batch_tokens and max_batch_size for those models
3) Short-term: evict large KV partitions and restart affected runtime pods if they don't release memory
Command I'm going to run (dry-run first):
```bash
redwoodctl runtime set-batching --model mistral-2.2-mqa --continuous false --max-batch-tokens 512 --max-batch-size 8 --region eu-west-1
redwoodctl runtime set-batching --model qwen-1.3-gqa --continuous false --max-batch-tokens 256 --max-batch-size 6 --region eu-west-1
```
Ingrid (Platform Eng): I'll prepare a rollout plan and watch autoscaler behavior. If we disable continuous batching, throughput will drop — need to ensure Dedicated customers on reserved capacity don't hit soft limits.
Luca (SRE): I'll stand by to scale up node count if CPU/burst queues spike after throttling. Also recommend a rolling restart of runtime pods to reclaim KV memory after eviction; will coordinate with deploy windows.
Emily (oncall): Go for the disable. Javier, run dry-run and then apply. Luca, be ready to scale. Ben, notify customers with a short note: "We're aware of intermittent timeouts for specific model variants in EU; mitigation in progress."
Deploy Bot: Started deployment pipeline: change-set for runtime-config
Javier (ML Infra): Applied: continuous batching disabled for mistral-2.2-mqa and qwen-1.3-gqa in eu-west-1 at 09:04:37 UTC. New batching policy committed (rev 2026.03.14-b2-revert).
Incident Bot: [INFO] config change applied to 12 runtime pods. Monitoring for 5m.
Ingrid (Platform Eng): After applying the change, KV cache cardinality stopped increasing in the shard logs. Example:```
[2026-03-14T09:06:12Z] model=mistral-2.2-mqa kv_cache_len=125400 -> 125410 -> 125412 (stabilized)
```
Luca (SRE): Despite stabilization, a few pods reported OOM events and were restarted. I've scaled up the node pool by +2 medium-gpus to absorb drop in batching efficiency.
Ben (Support): Customer update sent to impacted customers at 09:12 UTC. Two customers on Dedicated reported transient errors cleared after 09:10 UTC. Keeping them posted.
Customer Ops: Noting this for incident timeline. Any evidence this affected non-MQA/GQA variants?
Javier (ML Infra): Preliminary: only models with the MQA/GQA labeling and that matched the new aggressive thresholds were affected. Llama-based endpoints (llama-3 variants) not implicated. The root seems to be: threshold reduction allowed continuous batching to form very large virtual batch windows while prefix churn created near-unique KV keys per request, causing cache growth and memory exhaustion on long-tail clients.
Emily (oncall): Next steps?
Ingrid (Platform Eng): Actions to close incident:
- Rollback batching heuristic change in the release branch (done)
- Add safety guard to limit total new KV entries per minute per model (ticket created: INF-8321)
- Add telemetry for prefix-cardinality spikes and an alert when unique prefix keys > 50k/min per model (ticket INF-8322)
- Run a targeted eval suite against MQA/GQA prompt patterns to reproduce locally
Javier (ML Infra): Also pushing a temporary server-side mitigation: TTL on per-prefix cache entries reduced from 24h -> 30m for affected models to limit blowup. Patch applied at 09:18 UTC.
Luca (SRE): I'll produce a postmortem draft and include memory metrics and pod restart counts. ETA 24h. Assigning to me.
Deploy Bot: Noted deployment: ttl-change applied to 12 pods (09:18:07 UTC)
Emily (oncall): Handoff to next on-call: @luca_sre — I'll DM detailed notes. If anything re-escalates, wake me. Handoff time 09:20 UTC.
Luca (SRE): Acknowledged. I'll keep this thread open and update status.
Ben (Support): Customers on Dedicated asked for a root-cause statement; coordinated with Customer Ops to prepare a detailed post-incident message once postmortem is ready.
Customer Ops: We'll route drafts to legal/comms before sending. Thank you.
Javier (ML Infra): Long-term remediation ideas: smarter prefixed-key canonicalization to reduce artificial cardinality, model-specific batching profiles (don't treat MQA/GQA same as autoregressive Llama), and regression tests that run synthetic prefix-churn workloads in staging. Ticket set: INF-8323 (canonicalization), INF-8324 (model-specific profiles).
Incident Bot: [RESOLVED] Active alert cleared at 09:28:04 UTC. Continuous-batching disabled & TTL reduced; KV growth stabilized; customer errors returning to baseline. Please file postmortem within 48h.
Luca (SRE): Closing notes:
- Impact window: 08:58 UTC -> 09:28 UTC
- Root cause: aggressive continuous-batching heuristic combined with high prefix churn for MQA/GQA models leading to KV cache cardinality explosion -> memory pressure -> OOMs -> timeouts
- Immediate mitigations: rollback batching heuristic, disable continuous batching for affected models, reduce per-prefix TTL, scale nodes temporarily.
- Owners: Javier (temporary mitigation + long-term fixes), Ingrid (platform rollout + alerts), Luca (postmortem), Ben/Customer Ops (customer comms)
Emily (oncall): Thanks team. Good coordination. :thumbsup:
Luca (SRE): I'll post the postmortem link here when ready.
Deploy Bot: Deployment logs: change-set rev 2026.03.14-b2-revert + ttl-patch applied.
Incident Bot: Thread closed by Emily (oncall) at 09:50 UTC.
